PullRequest.Title: sessions: fix experimental composer picker positioning on phones
PullRequest.Body:

## Summary

Fixes a phone-layout regression following the composer unification in #342683. With `sessions.chat.experimental.newSessionComposerLayout` enabled, the picker tray inherited the mobile hero container’s expanding layout, separating it from the input.

- Keep the decorative logo in an independent flexible hero and dock the picker tray directly above the input.
- Keep notices above the pickers and hide the experimental composer’s empty bottom toolbar, which otherwise leaves an extra gap.
- Scope the new styling to the experimental phone layout; desktop and the standard phone composer retain their existing layout.
- Add geometry regression tests for short/tall phones, notices, setting toggles, desktop restoration, and empty/in-session states. Strengthen production component fixtures to require a flush tray on phones too.

- Keep enabled welcome phrases in normal flow above notices and pickers, without the legacy phone greeting offset. Both experimental phone fixtures now cover this default-enabled combination.

## Validation

Passed:

```sh
npm run build-fast -- --client-only
npm run compile-client
./scripts/test.sh --run src/vs/sessions/contrib/chat/test/browser/mobileChatShell.test.ts --run src/vs/sessions/test/browser/agentsPartCard.test.ts --run src/vs/sessions/contrib/chat/test/browser/chatView.test.ts --run src/vs/sessions/contrib/chat/test/browser/newSessionComposerLayout.test.ts --reporter dot
```

**198 tests passed.**

```sh
npm run eslint -- src/vs/sessions/contrib/chat/test/browser/mobileChatShell.test.ts src/vs/sessions/contrib/chat/test/browser/newChatWidget.fixture.ts
npm run stylelint -- src/vs/sessions/browser/parts/mobile/mobileChatShell.css
git diff --check
```

All passed; CSS lint reports existing advisory design-token suggestions.

Visually checked the real production composer’s 390px phone-layout component fixtures in dark/light themes with notices: tray and input have matching widths and a zero-pixel gap. Also inspected the native Code OSS Agents window on desktop. These are component-fixture checks, not physical-device testing.

## How to Test

1. On a phone, enable `sessions.chat.experimental.newSessionComposerLayout` and open a new session.
2. Confirm the workspace/repository picker tray sits flush above the input, with tips/notices above the tray and the logo in the remaining hero space.
3. Expand the tray and check it remains attached to the input.
4. Disable the setting, then check desktop separately: both should retain their previous layouts.

Scenarios.Scenario: Open a new session on a phone with the experimental composer enabled, including welcome text and optional notices
Scenarios.CriticalPath: DOM creation and existing composer initialization complete, then CSS style/layout/paint place the hero, notices, picker tray, and input. The changed work is confined to selector matching and one flex layout/paint pass on the visible composer.
Scenarios.ScalingInput: One new-session composer with one workspace-picker container, one existing logo pseudo-element relocated to the content container, and a small bounded set of notices/pickers; cost does not scale with session history or repository size.
Scenarios.EffectiveConcurrency: Single browser main-thread style/layout pass; no queue, parallel fan-out, limiter, or asynchronous work is introduced by the diff.
Scenarios.CacheBehavior: The same local SVG asset used before remains the logo source, so normal browser resource caching applies; the diff does not add cache keys, misses, retries, or invalidation behavior.
Scenarios.MechanismConfidence: High: the changed production hunk is CSS only, and surrounding construction code shows a single composer subtree and an existing ResizeObserver whose phone callback already avoids geometry reads. The new rules do not add script execution or boundary calls.
Scenarios.MagnitudeUncertainty: Exact style/layout duration varies by device, but the affected DOM cardinality is bounded and the diff replaces the prior pseudo-element rather than adding an additional visible logo.
Scenarios.Verdict: No reportable regression. The flex reordering and pseudo-element relocation cause bounded layout/paint work for one composer and do not create repeated synchronous reads, forced layout cycles, or scaling rendering work.

Scenarios.Scenario: Toggle the experimental composer setting or cross the phone/desktop breakpoint through rotation/resizing
Scenarios.CriticalPath: An existing autorun toggles the experimental class or the workbench toggles phone-layout; browser style recalculation and layout then apply or remove the changed rules. This style/layout work is on the visual transition path but remains one bounded subtree update per toggle/resize notification.
Scenarios.ScalingInput: One composer subtree per Agents window and user-driven setting/breakpoint changes, not per frame, row, history item, or repository.
Scenarios.EffectiveConcurrency: Serialized browser main-thread class update followed by style/layout; no newly introduced observer, timer, task burst, or concurrent resource creation.
Scenarios.CacheBehavior: No application cache participates. The local logo SVG remains reusable from the browser cache in both phone states, and desktop/no-agent/in-session selectors suppress the new pseudo-element.
Scenarios.MechanismConfidence: High: class toggle call sites and CSS scoping were traced; the diff adds no JavaScript callback and no transitive subprocess, IPC, filesystem, database, or network operation.
Scenarios.MagnitudeUncertainty: Device-specific recalc cost is unmeasured, but only a handful of selectors and elements are affected and transitions are infrequent.
Scenarios.Verdict: No reportable regression. The diff changes layout results when existing classes toggle without increasing event frequency or introducing forced synchronous geometry reads.

Scenarios.Scenario: Run component fixtures and the new mobile geometry regression suite
Scenarios.CriticalPath: Test setup constructs bounded synthetic DOM fixtures, then assertions synchronously read computed styles and bounding rectangles. These reads are test-only and do not affect product startup, interaction, or rendering paths.
Scenarios.ScalingInput: A fixed matrix of short/tall heights, notice presence, welcome visibility, and experimental/standard states; cardinality is constant in the checked-in suite.
Scenarios.EffectiveConcurrency: Tests execute according to the existing test runner; the diff adds no uncontrolled concurrency or product runtime work.
Scenarios.CacheBehavior: CSS and local SVG loading follow the existing test harness/browser cache behavior; no new cache or repeated remote fetch is introduced.
Scenarios.MechanismConfidence: High: the added TypeScript file is entirely under the test tree and its geometry reads are directly visible in the diff.
Scenarios.MagnitudeUncertainty: The exact CI runtime increment is not measured, but the fixed small test matrix cannot grow with user data and is not a user-visible product regression.
Scenarios.Verdict: No reportable product performance issue. Added test-only synchronous layout reads are fixed-cardinality validation work.

Analysis.Summary: Reviewed the complete four-file diff and traced the phone composer construction, class toggles, related base CSS, empty-toolbar handling, resize observer, and breakpoint helper. The only production changes are bounded CSS flex/order/display rules and relocation of an existing local-SVG pseudo-element. No hot-loop work, boundary fan-out, retention, concurrency burst, cache lifecycle issue, forced layout cycle, or concrete performance regression was introduced.
